where the products represent accumulated transmittance from the segment to the eye [S2, S3, unofficial].

The claim states that 'products represent accumulated transmittance from the segment to the eye'. Source [S2] provides the discrete equation where the term $e^{-k(s_0+j*Delta t)Delta t}$ is part of a product series $prod_{j=i+1}^n$. In the context of the integral $I(D) = I_0 e^{-int_{s_0}^D k(t) dt} + ...$, the exponential term $e^{-int} k(t) dt$ represents transmittance. The product of these exponentials for segments from the current sample $i$ to the end of the ray $D$ (the eye) represents the accumulated transmittance from that segment to the eye. Similarly, Source [S3] describes the attenuation term as a product series $prod_{j=0}^{i-1} e^{-mu(j Delta s) Delta s}$ which accumulates absorption (and thus transmittance) along the ray from the eye (start) to the current point. While S3 describes the product as accumulating from the eye to the segment, the claim specifically mentions 'from the segment to the eye', which aligns perfectly with the mathematical structure in S2 (and the physical definition of transmittance). Since S2 explicitly supports the interpretation of the product terms as accumulated transmittance from the segment to the eye (camera), the evidence supports the claim.

Source [S5] similarly defines $I_0$ as 'background intensity', states the first term represents 'occlusion of the background' (attenuated background), and the second term represents 'added intensity... as attenuated by the transparency'. All sources support the specific definitions and physical interpretations in the claim.
